findings.body: The database stores the scheme and path verbatim, while record_for_host compares only the parsed hostname, so migrated hosts no longer authorize embed requests.
findings.evidence: execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"
findings.failure_mode: Existing allowed hosts are silently converted into records that host_allowed? cannot find.
findings.impact: The database stores the scheme and path verbatim, while record_for_host compares only the parsed hostname, so migrated hosts no longer authorize embed requests.
findings.root_cause: The data migration uses raw SQL and bypasses the new model's before_validation normalization.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalize each legacy entry to its hostname (and supported port) before insertion, or insert through EmbeddableHost so its normalization callback runs.
findings.title: Legacy host entries are migrated without normalization
findings.trigger: Upgrade a site whose old embeddable_hosts setting contains entries such as http://eviltrout.com or https://example.com/1234, which the previous implementation accepted.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 25 inserts raw `h` values from the old site_setting without stripping scheme/path. The model's before_validation normalization only runs on ActiveRecord saves, not raw SQL. record_for_host compares URI.host against the stored value, so entries like 'http://eviltrout.com' won't match.

validated_findings.suggested_fix: Guard normalization with a presence check and let the existing format validation reject a missing host.
validated_findings.title: Missing host input causes a 500 instead of a validation error
validated_findings.trigger: Send an admin create or update request with embeddable_host[host] omitted or set to null.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 6 shows `self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` called unconditionally. If host is nil, sub! raises NoMethodError. No guard exists before this callback.

validated_findings.body: URI(host).host is example.com while the stored value includes :8080, so the lookup returns no record and the embed is rejected.
validated_findings.failure_mode: A syntactically valid configuration is treated as unauthorized at runtime.
validated_findings.impact: URI(host).host is example.com while the stored value includes :8080, so the lookup returns no record and the embed is rejected.
validated_findings.root_cause: The validation permits ports but record_for_host compares only URI.host against the full stored host string.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Normalize and compare host plus port consistently, or remove port support from the validation and stored format.
validated_findings.title: Configured hosts with ports can never authorize embeds
validated_findings.trigger: Configure a host such as example.com:8080 and send a referer from http://example.com:8080/....
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Validation regex allows ports (:[0-9]{1,5}), so 'example.com:8080' is valid and stored. record_for_host uses URI(host).host which returns 'example.com' without port, then compares against stored 'example.com:8080'. Mismatch causes lookup failure.

validated_findings.body: lower(host) is compared with the unlowercased URI host, so the configured record is not found and the request is rejected.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Equivalent hostname spellings produce inconsistent authorization results.
validated_findings.impact: lower(host) is compared with the unlowercased URI host, so the configured record is not found and the request is rejected.
validated_findings.root_cause: Only the database column is lowercased; the lookup value and model normalization are left case-sensitive.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Downcase the parsed host before binding it to the query and normalize stored hosts to lowercase.
validated_findings.title: Case-insensitive host matching is not actually case-insensitive
validated_findings.trigger: Store an allowed host with uppercase characters or send a referer such as HTTP://EVILTROUT.COM/....
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 17 uses `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` but the `host` variable from URI.host is not lowercased. If referer has uppercase (e.g., EVILTROUT.COM), URI.host preserves case, causing mismatch with lower(host) in DB.

validated_findings.body: categoryId remains null in the component, and this line overwrites the saved relationship with findById(null), so the category badge is blank and subsequent edits do not reflect the persisted category.
validated_findings.failure_mode: The persisted default category and the admin UI state diverge after a successful save.
validated_findings.impact: categoryId remains null in the component, and this line overwrites the saved relationship with findById(null), so the category badge is blank and subsequent edits do not reflect the persisted category.
validated_findings.root_cause: The client replaces the server-normalized category using the pre-save nullable UI value.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Use the category_id returned by the save response, update categoryId to that canonical value, and then resolve the category from it.
validated_findings.title: Saving a host without a category clears the displayed category
validated_findings.trigger: Add a host, leave the category chooser empty, and save it; the server defaults the missing category_id to the uncategorized category.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim assumes categoryId remains null after save. However, line 34 sets `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')` which is sent to server. Server defaults to uncategorized_category_id and returns it. The response hydrates category via rest_serializer. The UI issue is speculative without evidence the response isn't used.

validated_findings.body: record_for_host silently uses the first row, so the later relationship is ignored and embedded topics can be assigned to the wrong category; edits or deletes do not have an unambiguous effect.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Data configuration appears valid in the UI but runtime category selection depends on row order.
validated_findings.impact: record_for_host silently uses the first row, so the later relationship is ignored and embedded topics can be assigned to the wrong category; edits or deletes do not have an unambiguous effect.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new table has no uniqueness constraint and lookup resolves duplicates with first rather than rejecting them.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Normalize the host and add a case-insensitive uniqueness validation backed by a database unique index before allowing duplicate records.
validated_findings.title: Duplicate host records make category assignment ambiguous
validated_findings.trigger: An administrator creates the same hostname more than once with different categories, which the model and migration currently allow.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The finding describes a design limitation (no uniqueness constraint) rather than a bug introduced by this patch. The patch creates the table without unique constraint, but this is a design choice. The claim about ambiguous behavior is valid but is more of a missing feature than a defect.

validated_findings.body: The code either throws because null has no map method or replaces the original IDs with undefined relationship entries and then deletes the *_ids field.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Unrelated or partial REST payloads can crash hydration or silently discard relationship IDs.
validated_findings.impact: The code either throws because null has no map method or replaces the original IDs with undefined relationship entries and then deletes the *_ids field.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new generic *_ids branch assumes every plural ID field is an array-backed embedded association with a matching root collection.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Only hydrate plural IDs when the value is an array and the corresponding embedded collection exists; otherwise preserve the original *_ids field.
validated_findings.title: Plural ID hydration loses relationships when embedded collections are absent
validated_findings.trigger: Process a REST-serializer response containing a *_ids field without a corresponding root collection, or a null plural ID field.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 197 shows `obj[k].map(...)` where obj[k] could be null for a *_ids field. If a response has `foo_ids: null`, calling .map on null throws TypeError. The code assumes all *_ids fields are arrays.

validated_findings.body: host is nil and save_host dereferences it while assigning host.host, producing an internal server error instead of a not-found response.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Clients receive a 500 for a normal stale-resource request.
validated_findings.impact: host is nil and save_host dereferences it while assigning host.host, producing an internal server error instead of a not-found response.
validated_findings.root_cause: The update action converts a missing record into nil without handling that result.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Use find or explicitly return a 404 when the record is absent before calling save_host.
validated_findings.title: Updating a nonexistent embeddable host returns a 500
validated_findings.trigger: Send PUT /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id with an ID that does not exist.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Lines 10-11 show `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` then `save_host(host)`. If id doesn't exist, host is nil. save_host at line 23 does `host.host = ...` which raises NoMethodError on nil.

validated_findings.body: host.destroy is called on nil and raises NoMethodError instead of returning a not-found response.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Deleting a stale resource produces an unexpected server error.
validated_findings.impact: host.destroy is called on nil and raises NoMethodError instead of returning a not-found response.
validated_findings.root_cause: The destroy action does not check the result of the non-raising lookup.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Use find or explicitly handle a missing record before destroying it.
validated_findings.title: Destroying a nonexistent embeddable host returns a 500
validated_findings.trigger: Send DELETE /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id with an ID that does not exist.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Lines 15-16 show `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` then `host.destroy`. If id doesn't exist, host is nil and destroy raises NoMethodError.

validated_findings.body: Localized documentation continues to advertise settings that the migration deletes and that are no longer present in the settings configuration.
validated_findings.evidence: embeddable_hosts: "Host(s) that can embed the comments from this Discourse forum. Hostname only, do not begin with http://"
validated_findings.failure_mode: Administrators receive stale localization text and may search for unavailable settings.
validated_findings.impact: Localized documentation continues to advertise settings that the migration deletes and that are no longer present in the settings configuration.
validated_findings.root_cause: The patch deletes the English setting documentation but does not synchronize the translated locale files.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Remove or update the embeddable_hosts and embed_category entries in every locale file when removing those settings.
validated_findings.title: Non-English site-setting documentation still lists removed embedding settings
validated_findings.trigger: Use any non-English locale after this patch, where the corresponding server locale files still contain embeddable_hosts and embed_category descriptions.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The finding is about LEFT side (deleted line). The patch removes embeddable_hosts from server.en.yml. The claim about non-English locales is about files not modified by this patch - those are pre-existing issues, not introduced by this change.
